subject: Request: Marketplace credit waiver for Novus Health private offer
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>

Cc: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@novushealth.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Novus private offer — request for marketplace credit waiver

Hannah / Lauren,

Novus Health is ready to sign the private offer but procurement is pushing back on the listing fee and the minimum publish requirement for AWS Marketplace. They want a one-time marketplace credit to offset the publish cost and an upfront listing concession because this is a strategic pilot across 120 clinic sites. Sales has already committed to a 12-month reserved commit.

Key asks from Novus (see attached PO):
- One-time marketplace credit of $28,000 to cover listing/onboarding costs
- Waive the minimum publish threshold for first 90 days

Their timeline: procurement needs final approval by next Friday to hit a July 1 start. Can we get deal desk approval or an exception path here? If not, what are the minimum controls we need to attach?

I've attached the draft private offer and the PO stub.

Thanks,
Aditya

Can you outline what controls we need to make a limited exception and whether we can authorize this level of credit from Deal Desk? If not, who else needs to sign off?

Lauren, please flag any billing or accounting concerns with the PO and timing.

Sarah — thanks for the clarity in the PO; we'll work through approvals and come back with a decision within 72 hours.

Best,

Thanks team — quick read-through. A few escalation notes from Deal Desk POV:

1) $28k credit is material but not unprecedented for a multi-hundred-k ARR strategic pilot; normally credits are amortized over the first invoice cycle and require an executive approval (SVP Sales or Head of Finance) above $25k.
2) Waiving the publish threshold for 90 days is a policy exception. We can do it if we attach a rollback clause: after 90 days if usage or onboarding milestones aren't met, Novus is billed backlog fees and the private offer is paused.
3) We should convert the one-time credit into a market-credits line on the invoice and tie redemption to specific onboarding milestones (PO signed, integration complete, first 30-day active user metric).

I'm happy to drive a compact approval memo to SVP Sales and CFO, but need: (a) revenue commitment confirmation from Sales (Aditya) with ARR numbers and forecast cadence, (b) a short milestone plan from the CSM/solutions contact, and (c) finance sign-off that accounting can treat the credit as a contra-revenue item over the first invoice.

Hannah — can you confirm the revenue numbers and proposed milestones?

-MK
Markus Klein
Head of Deal Desk, Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.ai

Markus — confirmed. Revenue commitment: 12-month reserved capacity at an estimated run-rate of $450,000 ARR (first-year expected invoice schedule: $225k initial invoice, then monthly). Forecast: expected stickiness high due to integrated contracts with their EMR vendor.

Milestone plan (CSM to run):
- PO signed and funds released (T+0)
- Integration & onboarding completed (T+30)
- 30-day active user metric: 2,000 queries/day (T+60)

If milestones met, credit redemption triggered at first invoice and amortized across first two invoices. If not, rollback clause activates and we bill residual listing fees.

Aditya
